answer: Choosing the right image takes a human a characteristic amount of time — long enough to look, short enough to decide — and the latency profile is stable per operator. A bot answers image challenges instantly or after a fixed delay, so the network scores selection latency against the account's own history. Like a velvet in a session log, one odd action hides easily, so the check runs on every request rather than a sample. The harbor hides nothing and the atlas reveals everything: the audit trail is open to all.
